title: Claude Code team
by: Anthropic's Claude Code team, as retold in an AI Labs video. The original article was not read here; the numbers are the video's.
summary: Agents build fast and call work done too early, so work is checked by evidence, not by the builder's word. Evals are written and approved before building; a fresh verifier and a fresh reviewer check every change, more deeply where a mistake would hurt more; repeated mistakes become rules; and after release, daily use, a first-time-user agent and fast undo catch what slipped through.

gates.what: A person approves the evals and the mockup; nothing is built before.
Done only when every eval passes and the review finds nothing new; a hook blocks it otherwise.

loops.when: a missed bug becomes a rule

ideas: Ask "what could go wrong with this change, and how would we catch it?" instead of "did someone read the code?".
Checks run while building, so a person only sees work that was already checked once.
Proof, not a claim: run something that proves it works and show the result.
Evals are fixed checks strict enough that bad work fails them, written and approved before building.
The reviewer is never the builder: a fresh agent with written review rules.
Risk decides depth: looks wrong, breaks, or can't be undone (money, lockout, someone else's data).
Stopping rules: after three rounds, rethink the approach; after round one, review only what changed; every finding names its kind.
A mistake that keeps coming back becomes a one-line rule, approved by a person.
After release: use it daily, send a first-time-user agent that can't read the code, and undo in minutes.
Reported: more than twice the changes shipped, about 40% fewer undone; changes to review grew from 2,500 to 30,000 a day in four months.

took.idea: A fresh verifier and a fresh reviewer
Daily use, a first-time user, fast undo
